title: The afternoon a wall of dirt blacked out Kansas 🌪️
subject: duststorm
description:
Could a storm like Black Sunday happen again today? 👇

On April 14, 1935, a dust cloud up to 600 feet tall hit Dodge City, Kansas, at 50 to 60 mph and turned afternoon into night across the Great Plains. It was the worst of the Dust Bowl storms that pushed about 3.5 million people off the Plains.

Sources: National Weather Service Dodge City ("Black Sunday 1935"), National Weather Service Norman ("April 14, 1935 Black Sunday"), UT Austin EarthDate ("Dust Bowl 2"), Wikipedia ("Dust Bowl", "Black Sunday (storm)")

scenes.text: At 3 p.m., Dodge City went dark.
On April 14, 1935, a cloud of dust up to 600 feet tall rolled over Kansas at 60 mph.
In Amarillo, visibility was zero for 12 minutes. One woman remembered, "We stood in our living room in pitch blackness."
A year earlier, one storm had dropped 12 million pounds of dust on Chicago, then reached New York and Washington.
By 1940, about 3.5 million people had left the Plains.
